title: A project installation: the owned root in the project, referred to from omp's project plugin directory, binding no models
situation: Decision 0311 realized the project scope and wrote a project installation's tier models into the project's settings. The architect has since settled that a project installation binds no models: a tier's model is each operator's own setting, and a project installation is shared through the project. Review and use also showed that a project uninstall leaves behind the empty `.omp/` directory install created.
decision: As 0311, with (5) replaced and (10) added. (1) install and uninstall take `--scope user|project`, user by default; on a terminal install asks for the scope it is not told, user preselected, wherever the project resolved from the working directory is not the home; `--yes` or no terminal takes user. (2) The project is the one omp anchors its plugins at from the working directory: the nearest ancestor holding `.omp/` other than the home, else the nearest holding `.git`, else the working directory; project scope is refused where that is the home. (3) A project's owned root is `<project>/.cratylus/<harness>`, laid out as the user's, and its installation record states its scope. (4) Its references are in `<project>/.omp/plugins`, each relative: a link `node_modules/cratylus-omp` to the root, a relative `file:` dependency entry in that directory's `package.json`, and one `.gitignore` block, owned by its exact content, re-including that link. (5) A project install neither asks for nor writes any model role, in the project or anywhere else; `--model-roles` at project scope is refused, naming the user scope; it reads, without writing, the project's and the user's settings and names each tier neither binds as the operator's next step, to bind at user scope. The status line choice at project scope stays the project's `.omp/config.yml`. (6) A project install or uninstall writes nothing under the home. (7) The version-skew warning and report name the scope and root, and the remedy names its scope. (8) The operator's command, with no installation named, reads the nearest project installation above the working directory, else the user's. (9) Install refuses a project root over an author's render tree, and `project` refuses to render over an installation. (10) A project uninstall also removes the project's `.omp/` directory where install created it and it is left empty.
consequences: One builder; review Ask. The command reference's model-role and project-scope text changes with it.
